reason: B is more physically credible and testable because it links measurable dislocation-density/lattice-strain evolution to bounded changes in work hardening and high-temperature recovery, with in situ measurements that can falsify the mechanism. It is still weakened by annealing confounds and by partly restating prior evidence that residual cold-work dislocations cause hardening, whereas A relies on poorly justified element-wise thermal-expansion mismatch within a solid solution and predicts lower 1250 °C creep without a sound causal basis.
